title: Admired trumpeters: Cuckoo, Dumaine, Duran, Perez, Kid Rena
summary: Ferbos recalls hearing Louis Dumaine, Maurice Durand, Manuel Perez and Kid Rena; Dejan tells of Rena's stamina at the Gypsy Tea Room.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Mm-hm. You know it might seem odd, but at that time, for like, what's his name? Cuckoo. Cuckoo. You know I used to like to hear Cuckoo play. And then now the Cuckoo is- Well Cuckoo was a pretty good trumpet. Yeah, he was a pretty good trumpet at that time. And what was his set up for there? Louis Dumaine. And the set up when he used to work at the Broom place there. Maurice Duran. Maurice Duran. Yeah, I was proud of him.
He used to play in the alley right by the Seminole Market on the side that was the alley. And quite nice to know. The cab right there, he called it the alley.

And on the dry too? He was a top man. It was nice to sit in the shore, he used to play the lyrics, sit in the shore and then listen down and play. And it was Mayor Perez, he was the first one to start that wild wild music. I mean, and Buzz had picked it up after that, but he was the one who would really make it.

In other words, I mean, which is, honestly, what do you mean like street advertisements and we used to hear that at that time, you know, that maybe you want to ask them on that. Did you ever work on the street at that time? No, in the bands.
What band you like on the advertisements? You know, I used to play the advertisements like, you know, Gilbert Renier, Chris Kelly,

Punch and all that. Oh yeah, like, well, Kid Renier was another one. It was a pleasure. I mean, he was in the top lot. Oh yeah, he was a pleasure. You know, the first time I heard Kid Renier it was really odd. I had been hearing about Kid Renier for years. And when I heard him and I saw him, in fact, he didn't even seem to be a type of man to me. I thought he was a great big fella, the way he used to talk about him, but he was a very small fella. Yes, he got him to take. And when I heard him play, so I asked a lot of fun, I said, well, I said, that man's a real Trump player, who is he? He said, you don't know that, that's Kid Renier. Yeah, he really was a fine Trump player. You remember him?
Oh yeah, I mean, did you hear him when he was in his head there?
No, but he came back on two numbers and really cut those.
Oh, he was a fine Trump player.

I couldn't believe it. All of a sudden, he just took five. When we were playing at the Gypsy Tea Room, Don Redmond come down with that big, beautiful, fine band out of New York, and he had a lovely big band, a 16 piece band, and we had I think six pieces. And Don Redmond said, hi in the world, can that trumpet player play all night like that, and it don't ever look like he get tired. Every number Kid Renier played was just like, the last number was like the first number.

Yeah, he was a good trumpet player. See, the fellas, what he was talking, first, I mean, there's first class musicians. I just broke it down. You know, the ordinary fellas, like what I'm talking about, Chris Kelly time. I don't remember Chris Kelly really.
